import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import io

# Dataset provided as a string
data = """Person ID,Gender,Age,Occupation,Sleep Duration,Quality of Sleep,Physical Activity Level,Stress Level,BMI Category,Blood Pressure,Heart Rate,Daily Steps,Sleep Disorder
1,Male,27,Software Engineer,6.1,6,42,6,Overweight,126/83,77,4200,
2,Male,28,Doctor,6.2,6,60,8,Normal,125/80,75,10000,
3,Male,28,Doctor,6.2,6,60,8,Normal,125/80,75,10000,
4,Male,28,Sales Representative,5.9,4,30,8,Obese,140/90,85,3000,Sleep Apnea
5,Male,28,Sales Representative,5.9,4,30,8,Obese,140/90,85,3000,Sleep Apnea
"""

# Read the data into a pandas DataFrame
df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(data))

# Set a clean style for seaborn plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create a figure and axes for the plot
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 7))

# Create a scatter plot to visualize the relationship between Sleep Duration and Quality of Sleep,
# using BMI Category for color and Stress Level for marker size.
# This helps in understanding how different BMI categories and stress levels relate to sleep patterns.
scatter_plot = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='Sleep Duration',
    y='Quality of Sleep',
    hue='BMI Category',       # Color points by BMI Category
    size='Stress Level',      # Size points by Stress Level (higher stress = larger point)
    sizes=(100, 800),         # Range of marker sizes
    palette='viridis',        # Colormap for hue
    alpha=0.8,                # Transparency of points
    edgecolor='w',            # White edge around points
    linewidth=1               # Width of the edge
)

# Add title and labels for clarity
plt.title('Sleep Duration vs. Quality of Sleep by BMI Category and Stress Level', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Sleep Duration (hours)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Quality of Sleep (1-10)', fontsize=12)

# Improve legend placement and appearance
plt.legend(title='BMI Category', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0.)

# Adjust layout to prevent labels from overlapping
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the plot as output.png
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300)
